scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The tourdion originated in the Burgundian court in the mid-15th century and remained popular in France until the late-16th century.
It is documented in early treatises such as Antonius de Arena's 1519 Ad suos compagnos and Thoinot Arbeau's 1589 Orchésographie.
on_screen: Map: France · Europe
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The tourdion served as a social court dance, often performed as the second part of a dance suite following a basse danse to provide a contrast in tempo.
Today it is a historical tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Medieval Music vol.3 (1000-1450) (https://archive.org/details/youtube-I8CW7P4k7II)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is based on the 'cinq pas' (five-step) sequence.
It involves alternating between 'posture droit' and 'posture gauche,' utilizing 'pied en l'air' (kicks) and 'petit saut' (small hops), concluding with a 'saut moyen' to transition postures.
Watch for Cinq pas, Saut moyen.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (J-_ZJZhwC84)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Couple dance, moving through the space.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is in triple meter and is characterized by a rapid, light tempo.
It was frequently published for lute or as four-part vocal arrangements, most notably in the 1530 collections by Pierre Attaingnant.
Listen for the Lute, Voice.
The pulse is Triple meter.
A brisk, triple-meter melody that feels lighter and more concise than the galliard, often featuring repetitive, danceable phrases.

Listen later: La Magdalena — Pierre Attaingnant (collection)

scenes.title: The people
narration: Pierre Attaingnant (publisher), Thoinot Arbeau (theorist), Antonius de Arena (theorist), César Geoffray (arranger).
Known as 'tordiglione' or 'dordiglione' in Italy, where it featured more ornate, improvised footwork as documented by Caroso and Negri.
Related to the galliard, sharing similar musical airs but differing in the height and intensity of the steps.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Tourdion is sibling of Galliard: Shares the same musical air but differs in tempo and the height of the jumps.
Tourdion is shares music of Basse danse: Often paired with the tourdion due to their contrasting tempi.

scenes.title: Try one step
narration: Before we go, one step. Assume posture gauche (left foot forward, weight even).
Perform a pied en l'air droit (right foot kick) with a simultaneous petit saut (small hop) on the left foot.
Count it: count the Triple meter bar out loud, then in pairs of bars.
Chapter 1 takes it slowly from here.
